text.p: Germany's Daimler-Benz AG, maker of luxury Mercedes cars, said Thursday it was recalling 176,000 vehicles worldwide due to problems with their braking systems.
The brakes could overreact to a slight push on the brake pedal, a spokesman said. The cars need to be brought to garages for new components to be installed.
The brake system problem affects a series of Mercedes models, and was first noticed in the S-class luxury saloon, and the SL cabriolet at the end of 1996.
Since March, the E-class executive range, and since June, the C-class sedan and CLK cabriolet have also been diagnosed with the defect.
The spokesman said that new brake sensors were now being built into cars under production.

The Mercedes braking system was designed to recognise emergency situations and engage at full power, the spokesman said. But accident research has shown that drivers often do not step on the brakes hard enough to avoid accidents, he added.
Of the total, about 88,000 of the affected vehicles are in Germany.
